description: [allAfrica] In Gidan Dare, a farming community near the BUA Cement plant in northwest Nigeria, residents describe wells that once reached water at three or four metres now requiring seventy or more metres before anyone strikes anything.
title: Africa: Climate Finance Needs Proof, not Promises

description: [Ghanaian Times] Antalya, TÜRKİYE -- The Minister for Environment, Science and Technology, Dr Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings, has urged African countries to strengthen their collective voice in international climate negotiations to demand climate justice, equitable access to climate finance and fair trade arrangements for the continent's critical minerals.
title: Africa: Africa Must Speak With One Voice On Climate Finance - Minister

description: [RootsToFoods Capital Series] In a RootsToFoods Capital Series interview, AfricInvest co-founder Ziad Oueslati explains how a Tunis-born private equity fund manager managing a $10 million first fund in 1994 became a pan-African platform, and why local teams, hands-on equity and blended structures are what move institutional capital.
title: Africa: How Africa's Private Equity Industry Was Built on Local Trust

description: [New Era] BEIJING -- An African media delegation from nine countries, including Namibia, has explored how news organisations are adapting to artificial intelligence (AI) during a visit to the People's Daily in Beijing, China.
title: Africa: China - Africa Explore Ai-Powered Media Futures

title: Africa: World Governments Summit Sets Agenda for Latin America and Caribbean Talks

description: [African Development Bank (AfDB)] The African Development Bank Group (Bank Group) and the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) are looking to broaden their partnership in support of Africa's development, following talks between their leaders on 13 November.
title: Africa: The African Development Bank Group and JICA Explore New Avenues of Cooperation for Africa

description: [IPS] Antalya, Türkiye &amp; Sonipat, India -- "Climate action has to deliver where people live," COP31 President Murat Kurum said on Resilient Cities and Built Environment Day, part of the Leaders Summit. Cities, he said, are "where that implementation becomes real - in the homes people live in, the infrastructure they depend on and the energy they use every day."
title: Africa: COP31 - Leaders Put Resilient Cities On the Table. Will the Money Follow?

description: [IPS] Antalya, Türkiye -- When unpredictable rainfall, rising temperatures and declining soil fertility threatened agricultural production across Nigeria four years ago, Baliqees Salaudeen-Ibrahim turned to biofertilisers to keep soil healthy, sustain her horticultural production and build resilience against the growing effects of climate change.
title: Africa: How Biofertilisers Help African Farmers Adapt to Climate Change

description: [SAnews.gov.za] Africa must build the digital infrastructure of the future, invest in its people and nurture African innovation ecosystems if it is to become a competitive force in the global Artificial Intelligence (AI) economy, says Deputy President Paul Mashatile.
title: Africa: Africa Urged to Build the Digital Future, Not Just Consume It

description: [UNITAID] Unitaid welcomes Gilead's announcement of royalty-free voluntary licensing agreements with Dr. Reddy's Laboratories, Eva Pharma and Ferozsons Laboratories. The agreements lay the groundwork for wider access to obeldesivir, an investigational antiviral being studied to prevent Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD). If clinical evidence supports its use and regulators approve it, the three manufacturers across different regions will be able to produce and supply obeldesivir in the 127 countries covered by
title: Africa: Access Planning for Ebola Medicines Moves Ahead During Clinical Trials

description: [UNITAID] Unitaid is investing US$28.6 million to expand access to testing for multiple diseases. Through two complementary projects led by the Aurum Institute and Benin's National Tuberculosis Program, the investment will explore how countries can better connect diagnostic services, identify conditions that might otherwise go undetected and help more people get the tests and care they need.
title: Africa: Unitaid Launches U.S.$28.6 Million Investment to Integrate Diagnostic Services and Expand Access to Care

title: Africa: All of Africa Today - November 18, 2026

description: [WHO] The Government of Spain and 20 other countries today joined the World Health Organization (WHO) and UNICEF to launch the global call to action on obesity, "Bending the curve by 2030". The participating governments committed to accelerate prevention, early intervention and care, and to reduce national obesity prevalence by 5% by 2030.
title: Africa: Leaders Commit to Accelerate Action On Obesity Prevention and Control

description: [WHO] Governments are stepping up action to protect children from violence, with over 230 new pledges to be announced at the Second Global Ministerial Conference on Ending Violence Against Children in Manila, Philippines taking place on 18-19 November, the World Health Organization (WHO) said today.
title: Africa: Governments Make Over 230 New Pledges to Prevent Violence Against Children

description: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- A coalition of Horn of Africa diaspora communities staged a protest outside the U.S. Department of State in Washington, D.C., on Monday, November 16, calling on the United States and the international community to intervene over ongoing conflicts in Ethiopia and mounting regional tensions.
title: Africa: Washington Protest Brings Horn of Africa Diaspora Over Ethiopia Conflicts, Regional Instability

description: [UN News] From identifying marine life with a cup of seawater to drawing on Indigenous knowledge to prevent wildfires, scientists and communities showcased both cutting-edge and time-tested ways to protect nature at COP31 on Tuesday. Yet turning innovation into action remains a challenge, with funding gaps persisting and ministers struggling to bridge divisions over fossil fuels and climate finance as negotiations enter their final days.
title: Africa: COP31 - the Push to Protect Warming Oceans Reaches the Negotiating Table

description: [IPS] Antalya, Türkiye -- The world is moving dangerously close to irreversible climate tipping points, making urgent action to reduce greenhouse gas emissions more critical than ever, warns Johan Rockström, Director of the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research. He argues that protecting forests and accelerating emissions reductions must go hand in hand to prevent further warming and preserve the planet's natural capacity to absorb carbon dioxide.
title: Africa: COP31 - Johan Rockström Warns of Climate Tipping Points and Efforts to Sideline Science

title: Africa: An African Institution Will Not Be Put On Trial By Anonymous Sources and Politically Motivated Journalists

description: [Africa CDC] As external health financing declines and public health threats persist, Africa's flagship public health conference will examine progress, confront remaining gaps and advance African-led solutions.
title: Africa: CPHIA 2026 - African Leaders to Convene in Addis Ababa to Advance Health Security and Sovereignty

description: [Africa CDC] In late November 2026, Addis Ababa will host the 5th International Conference on Public Health in Africa (CPHIA 2026), co-convened by the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) and the Government of Ethiopia. Its theme, 'Africa's Health Security and Sovereignty: Transformation from health dependency and vulnerability to ownership and resilience', states its intent.
title: Africa: From Dependency to Sovereignty - What the International Conference On Public Health in Africa 2026 Must Deliver for Africa's Health Security
